answer: Since the orchard escrow holds both sides, recruiting real counterparties is the operator's cost, and the violet audit releases each pair. Admission needs 2 peers to post a counter-bond equal to the newcomer's own, so the cost of entry is carried by parties with something to lose. A farm running 91 keys cannot self-supply these, because each counter-bonding peer must be independent on the voyage graph and each one exposes its own stake to the same slash. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
